recentlyRead.title: A Deadly Education
recentlyRead.author: Naomi Novik
recentlyRead.review: pretty interesting magic system but i wish it was less school-focused.

recentlyRead.title: Bird by Bird
recentlyRead.author: Anne Lamott
recentlyRead.review: this was ok. there were a few gems in it that helped me to better understand the writing process and develop my own, but at times it read more like an autobiography. at first, the book feels heavily influenced by religion, but thankfully Anne’s life has been so colorful that it wasn’t too cringe worthy and veered towards entertaining. her advice on publishing was very one-note, and not something i found valuable or cared for, and some of her tools like KFKD were not necessary/could have been omitted. if you are interested in writing or in the process of writing from an autobiographical lens, then this is a worthwhile read and feels accurate.

recentlyRead.title: Carrie
recentlyRead.author: Stephen King
recentlyRead.review: i enjoyed reading Carrie because it is fast-paced and a unique storytelling style. i did not like the lack of chapters; it made it difficult to stop and remember where i left off. the newspaper clippings and secondary accounts were, at first, confusing, but in the end dovetailed nicely.

recentlyRead.title: The Elements of Style
recentlyRead.author: William Strunk Jr.
recentlyRead.review: very informative but also a dry read. if you’re looking for the information in this, but would prefer a little more “life” to the writing, i recommend Stephen King’s “On Writing”—it contains the most important bits and is enthralling.

recentlyRead.title: Hard Drive: Bill Gates and the Making of the Microsoft Empire
recentlyRead.author: James Wallace
recentlyRead.review: definitely a few things in here about Bill that are not common knowledge while being interesting to read. a definitive history of early Microsoft and Gates himself for those curious but not at the level of an Isaacson.

recentlyRead.title: Unbroken Brain: A Revolutionary New Way of Understanding Addiction
recentlyRead.author: Maia Szalavitz
recentlyRead.review: interesting tidbit about her life but later chapters were markedly less scintillating to the point i considered not finishing. overall fairly autobiographical (which is what i was looking for) and some helpful science.

recentlyRead.title: The Self Delusion: The New Neuroscience of How We Invent―and Reinvent―Our Identities
recentlyRead.author: Gregory Berns
recentlyRead.review: a helpful reframe of the present, future, and past self. salient points include you can and often are whoever you want to be through the stories you tell and the decisions you make and we are our own hero’s journey.

recentlyRead.title: Trivergence: Accelerating Innovation with AI, Blockchain, and the Internet of Things
recentlyRead.author: Bob Tapscott
recentlyRead.review: everything in this book one can glean by having a reasonable intuition about the current tech scene. i suppose it would be valuable if you do not. in any case, it reads like it was AI generated…

recentlyRead.title: On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft
recentlyRead.author: Stephen King
recentlyRead.review: really enjoyed this. so much so that i went and bought the first three books Stevie published: Carrie, ‘Salem’s Lot, and The Shining. i am looking forward to reading them next.

recentlyRead.title: How to Navigate Life: The New Science of Finding Your Way in School, Career, and Beyond
recentlyRead.author: Belle Liang
recentlyRead.review: some interview tips are helpful but generally the archetypes mentioned are uninspired. advice about improving one’s life is basic and rather trope-y.

recentlyRead.title: How to Win Friends & Influence People
recentlyRead.author: Dale Carnegie
recentlyRead.review: was ok. lots of the content is out of date historically but the concepts still hold true though not sure how effective they actually are.

recentlyRead.title: Dopamine Nation: Finding Balance in the Age of Indulgence
recentlyRead.author: Anna Lembke
recentlyRead.review: an excellent education for those looking to understand addiction at its roots and the effects it has on individuals, groups, and society.

recentlyRead.title: Jewels: A Secret History
recentlyRead.author: Victoria Finlay
recentlyRead.review: interesting read and helpful knowledge but a little dry at times.

recentlyRead.title: Homo Deus: A History of Tomorrow
recentlyRead.author: Yuval Noah Harari
recentlyRead.review: pretty good but not anywhere near sapiens.

recentlyRead.title: The Scaling Era: An Oral History of AI, 2019–2025
recentlyRead.author: Dwarkesh Patel
recentlyRead.review: was an interesting read with a number of helpful topics regarding the latest developments in Al and the infrastructure required to power it. at times, the Q/A-style with lots of references and sub-text was trying but otherwise pleasant and educational. it is approachable for those that are not technical and does a good job of explaining esoterica.

recentlyRead.title: The Last Graduate
recentlyRead.author: Naomi Novik
recentlyRead.review: Not as good as the first book.

recentlyRead.review: i read this in high school and it was ok. i read it again recently and it was much better than i remembered. the writing is beautiful and the story is tragic.

recentlyRead.title: A Game of Thrones
recentlyRead.author: George R.R. Martin
recentlyRead.review: a classic. Tyrion is my favorite character before you ask.

recentlyRead.title: Fablehaven
recentlyRead.author: Brandon Mull
recentlyRead.review: read this series as a preteeen and really enjoyed it. the world-building is fantastic and the characters are well-developed. the plot is engaging and keeps you hooked until the end.

recentlyRead.title: Jeremy Thatcher, Dragon Hatcher
recentlyRead.author: Bruce Coville
recentlyRead.review: Jeremy Thatcher, Dragon Hatcher is close to my heart as the first book i actually completed. i still fantisize about finding my own Mr. Elives' Magic Shop. i highly reccomend it to young readers who are struggling to find their footing in the world of books.

recentlyRead.title: The Alchemyst
recentlyRead.author: Michael Scott
recentlyRead.review: this was the second series i read after Harry Potter that really engaged and intersted me. i especially enjoyed the reference to the real historical figures and events. the story is well-written and the characters are likable. you'll be wishing you got a summer job and ended up an alchemists's apprentice after reading this.

recentlyRead.title: Intuition Pumps and Other Tools for Thinking
recentlyRead.author: Daniel C. Dennett
recentlyRead.review: great mental and logic hacks to help you think more clearly and effectively. the book is well-written and easy to understand, making it accessible to a wide audience. highly recommend for anyone looking to improve their critical thinking skills.

recentlyRead.title: Clarity & Connection
recentlyRead.author: Yung Pueblo
recentlyRead.review: my first real foray into poetry and i really enjoyed it. the poems are simple but profound, and they really resonated with me. i would recommend this book to anyone looking for a little bit of inspiration and wisdom in their life.
